verses.text: “I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask. I am found by those who didn’t seek me. I said, ‘See me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name.
I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;
a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks;
who sit among the graves, and spend nights in secret places; who eat pig’s meat, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
who say, ‘Stay by yourself, don’t come near to me, for I am holier than you.’ These are smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all day.
“Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will repay, yes, I will repay into their bosom,

your own iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together”, says Yahweh, “who have burned incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills. Therefore I will first measure their work into their bosom.”
Yahweh says, “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, ‘Don’t destroy it, for a blessing is in it:’ so will I do for my servants’ sake, that I may not destroy them all.
I will bring offspring  out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains. My chosen will inherit it, and my servants will dwell there.
Sharon will be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me.
“But you who forsake Yahweh, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny;

I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you didn’t answer. When I spoke, you didn’t listen; but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”

Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed;
Behold, my servants will sing for joy of heart, but you will cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for anguish of spirit.
You will leave your name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord Yahweh will kill you. He will call his servants by another name,

so that he who blesses himself in the earth will bless himself in the God of truth; and he who swears in the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.
“For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.
But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a joy.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying will be heard in her no more.

“No more will there be an infant who only lives a few days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old will be accursed.
They will build houses, and inhabit them. They will plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
They will not build, and another inhabit. They will not plant, and another eat: for the days of my people will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands.
They will not labor in vain, nor give birth for calamity; for they are the offspring  of Yahweh’s blessed, and their descendants with them.
It will happen that, before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says Yahweh.

footnotes.content: Here is the heart of grace: the Lord seeking those who didn't ask, found by those who didn't seek. He must cry out 'See me, see me' to get our notice—not because He's loud, but because we're deaf to anything but our own noise. Yet He keeps calling, patient as only the eternal can be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All day He spreads out His hands—that gesture of offer, of embrace, of vulnerability. The image carries forward to Calvary. A rebellious people walk their own way, and still His hands remain open, always open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They provoke Him to His face: burning incense in gardens instead of the temple, worshiping in secret places. It's not just disobedience—it's a kind of mocking, a deliberate turning away that says, 'We know You're there, and we choose this instead.' The cruelty of that choice wounds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sitting among graves, eating unclean things—the details matter. They've embraced death, not just in worship but in daily living. They're not seeking life anymore; they're rehearsing its loss. This is what happens when a people forgets that holiness points toward life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Stay away—I'm holier than you,' they sniff, even as they sit among the dead. Pride wraps itself in ritual and calls it purity. To the Lord, it's smoke in His nostrils, offensive and stale—the smoke that doesn't rise toward heaven but drifts around us, poisoning what we touch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It is written before Him—not a record He's keeping to embarrass us later, but truth He sees clearly now. He will repay not out of anger but out of justice, the way a parent must finally let a child feel the weight of choices made against all warning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The iniquities of fathers and children together—not because the children are blamed for their parents' sins, but because they chose the same path. Each generation has the chance to turn; each generation that refuses compounds the weight. Yet even here, judgment is measured 'into their bosom'—not erasure, not extinction, but reckoning they can still understand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new wine found in the cluster—when one says 'Don't destroy it, for a blessing is in it,' we hear the vintner's care. So the Lord speaks: for My servants' sake, I will spare. Even judgment rests on mercy; even wrath remembers grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Offspring out of Jacob, inheritors of mountains—the promise shifts. Not the whole nation, but a remnant, God's chosen, will inherit. This is how grace works after judgment: it doesn't erase the past but opens a door through it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sharon becomes a fold for flocks, the valley of Achor (trouble, sorrow) becomes a place of rest. Names mean something here—the geography itself is redeemed. Places of old pain become places of peace for those who sought the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They prepare a table for Fortune and Destiny—lifting up strange gods with familiar names. In their minds, they're hedging their bets, covering their ground. But the Lord asks: will you forsake Me for luck? Will you choose blind fate over the God who knows you?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When I called, you didn't answer—the pattern closes. He called, they didn't listen. They did what was evil in His sight, choosing what He didn't delight in. Judgment follows not from harshness but from the simple weight of refusal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My servants will eat, you will be hungry—the contrast is stark and true. It doesn't come from divine spite but from the shape of things: those who seek the Lord find provision; those who turn away find emptiness. This is the covenant written into the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Servants sing for joy of heart; the others cry and wail. Notice the Lord doesn't force the tears—He simply lets the two paths reach their natural ends. Joy and sorrow spring from the same root: what we've chosen to love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your name becomes a curse; His servants He'll call by a new name. A name is identity, inheritance, promise. To lose it is to lose the thread that ties you to tomorrow. His chosen get a new thread, a new story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He who blesses himself will bless himself in the God of truth—a strange grace here. Even those who resist must eventually swear by what is real. The old troubles fade from His eyes; He doesn't rehearse them. Forgetting, for the Lord, is an act of love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, I create new heavens and new earth—the word is bara, creation from nothing. This isn't renovation; it's newness. Former things won't be remembered, not erased but truly gone, the way childhood fades when morning comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create—Jerusalem a delight, her people a joy. This is the end of all sorrow: not the absence of feeling but the presence of God's joy, so full that it crowds out everything else. Eternal not as duration but as the presence of what satisfies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No more weeping, no more crying—He says this not to deny that tears were real, but to say they were never meant to be the final word. The Lord will rejoice in His people. Even His delight is a thing worth hearing, like the echo of perfect homecoming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No infant dying young, no old person cut short—the restoration includes the arc of life as it should be. Even children born 'one hundred years old' speaks to a world where youth and age both belong, where fullness is measured not in speed but in completeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will build houses and inhabit them, plant vineyards and eat their fruit—the basic dignity of work that isn't stolen, of harvest that isn't taken away. Adam's labor without the curse, the fruit of hands that know they belong to something true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Days of my people will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands—security not from hoarding but from knowing the Lord. To enjoy the fruit of your work without fear of loss is to rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will not labor in vain, nor give birth for calamity—the promise of fruitfulness, not in the world's terms but in the Lord's eyes. Offspring of the blessed, descendants carrying blessing forward. The work matters because He sees it and holds it good.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before they call, I will answer; while they are yet speaking, I will hear. Readers today hear an echo of this: how often have you found that what you were about to ask for, the Lord had already begun to move toward you? Looking back from a longer road, I see His timing is always a breath ahead of ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wolf and lamb will feed together, lion eating straw like the ox, dust the serpent's food—creation restored, enemies reconciled, death itself diminished to dust. This is the end: not escape from the world but its healing, the kingdom come in fullness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
